display.purpose: The home headline; the help page title sits at its 34px floor.

headline.purpose: The one heading of a rail or workspace. The sentence being written uses the same size at weight 700.

figure.purpose: The single large tabular number in a rail: collected count, percent.

title.purpose: Dialog titles and help-page section headings.

body.purpose: Prose on ground or white, in ink-2, max 34em to 68ch.

label.purpose: Field labels, rail labels and notes, counts, captions. The smallest size.

shadows.name: input-focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Zero-blur ink ring on a focused text input. A line, not elevation.

shadows.name: empty-tile-outline
shadows.purpose: 1px inset outline on an empty jamo tile. A line, not elevation.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The one easing curve for entrances, hovers that move, and view-transition groups.

motion.name: control-transition
motion.purpose: Colour, border and transform on buttons and inputs; press scales to .97.

motion.name: progress-fill
motion.purpose: Progress indicator transform.

motion.name: vt-rail
motion.value: group 420ms on lime; old out 150ms ease-in (opacity 0, translateY -8px); new in 320ms ease-out-expo after 150ms (from opacity 0, translateY 10px)
motion.purpose: The lime rail holds still across flow routes while its contents change.

motion.name: vt-stage
motion.purpose: The white stage holds still across flow routes; contents cross-fade.

motion.name: vt-lead
motion.value: group 640ms ease-out-expo; old/new height 100%, width auto
motion.purpose: The lead glyph travels from the end of generation to the first typed character of the preview.

motion.name: vt-root
motion.purpose: Cross-fade for everything outside the named parts.

motion.name: lead-in
motion.purpose: The finished lead glyph appearing in the film's lime box.

motion.name: lead-hold
motion.purpose: How long the finished lead glyph is held before the preview takes over (0 under reduced motion).

motion.name: film-full-cues
motion.purpose: Start of each of the first seven steps in the full generation film.

motion.name: film-short-cues
motion.value: opens on step 6; field at 1.5s; may finish at 3s
motion.purpose: The short film played on regeneration.

motion.name: film-sibling-interval
motion.purpose: Interval between sibling syllables in the composition step.

motion.name: film-progress-follow
motion.value: exponential approach, 120ms time constant; worker progress 3-94% mapped to 0-1
motion.purpose: How the 11,172 field follows real progress at any frame rate.

motion.name: film-step-ease
motion.purpose: Quartic ease-out for pose changes inside the film.

motion.name: type-interval
motion.purpose: The typing arrival on the preview page.

motion.name: caret
motion.purpose: Blinking ink caret during the typing arrival.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Sample rows arriving after the sentence has typed.

motion.name: tile-in
motion.purpose: A newly collected jamo tile.

motion.name: combo
motion.value: 420ms ease-out-expo; glyph from scale .9, tile from translateY 70%; one change every 1500ms
motion.purpose: The home combination demonstration.

motion.name: sample-row-hover
motion.purpose: Hover on a preview sample row.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animations and transitions .01ms, one iteration; view transitions none; film kind 'none' (field only, no skip, no hold); no typing arrival; home demo static
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion behaviour.

narrative.overview:
OwnChar draws like a sequential-pose pictogram: one subject, shown again and again in a new pose, never swapped for something else. The subject is the writer's own handwriting. It is written on a white stage, and from that point on it stays on screen: lifted out of its sentence, steadied, outlined, split into jamo, brought to one size, recombined, multiplied to 11,172 syllables, and finally typed back as a sentence. No page in the flow replaces the handwriting with a spinner or an illustration of progress; the handwriting is the progress.

The palette is three values on a quiet ground: ink, white, and one lime field. Everything is flat. Lime is a surface that frames the work (the flow rail, the editor bar, the home demonstration); white is where the work happens; solid ink marks whatever is selected, live, or primary. Hierarchy comes from weight and from reversing ink and lime, not from more colours or more sizes. Corners are 6px, lines are 1px.

The system is dense and tool-like in the stage and calm in the rail. It avoids paper or stationery imitation, the white-and-blue SaaS tool shell, and a dark technical look; those were ruled out by the user when this world was chosen.
keyCharacteristics: Ink, white, one lime field, on a warm-neutral ground; one red for destruction and errors only.
A fixed frame for the main flow: lime rail at the left, white stage for the rest, primary action at the rail's bottom.
Solid ink is the single mark of "selected / current / primary".
Flat: no elevation shadows, no tonal gradients, 1px hairlines, 6px corners.
Two sans families: IBM Plex Sans KR for the page h1 only, Noto Sans KR for all other interface text; the user's handwriting font is the only other typeface that ever appears.
Motion keeps things in place and changes their pose; route changes hold the rail and stage and move one glyph across.

rules.name: The Solid Ink Rule
rules.body: Selection, the live step, progress, and the primary action are solid ink with white text. If two things on one surface are solid ink, one of them is wrong, unless one is a toggle that is on.

rules.name: The Lime Is A Field Rule
rules.body: Lime is a surface or a tint, never a text colour on white or ground (1.3:1). Lime text exists only on solid ink: the number of the current step, the count in the current rail row, the boundary notice on the ink bar, the dot in the logo mark.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Red means "this destroys work" or "this failed". It is never decoration, never a badge, never a second accent.

rules.name: The Few Sizes Rule
rules.body: 12, 14, 16, 18, 26, 44 and the display clamp. A new level of hierarchy is a weight change or an ink/lime reversal before it is a new size.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes (counts, percent, px values, slider readouts) is tabular and non-wrapping.

rules.name: The Korean Line Rule
rules.body: Text breaks between words, not inside them (`word-break: keep-all`), and headings are balanced.

rules.name: The Same Place Rule
rules.body: A page in the write → generate → preview flow uses the rail-and-stage frame, puts its primary action at the rail's bottom, and names its rail `rail` and its stage `stage` so the frame holds across the navigation.

rules.name: The Never Cut Rule
rules.body: Waiting is shown on the user's own strokes, driven by real progress. No spinner, no skeleton, no stand-in illustration.

rules.name: The Flat Field Rule
rules.body: Depth is a change of field or a hairline. If a surface needs a shadow to read as separate, give it a border in ink or rule instead.

dos: Do build a flow page from the frame: lime rail (280px, 1px ink right edge), white stage, primary action in solid ink at the rail's bottom.
Do mark the selected, current or pressed thing with solid ink and white text, and use lime text only on that ink.
Do use lime-ink for secondary text on lime and ink-2 / ink-3 for secondary text on white and ground.
Do keep every control at a 6px corner (4px when nested), every structural line at 1px ink, every quiet line at 1px rule.
Do show any wait or computation on the user's own strokes and drive it from real progress.
Do carry a navigation inside the flow with the `rail`, `stage` and `lead` transitions, and keep every animation on `cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)`.
Do give every animated behaviour a still equivalent under reduced motion that shows the same information.
Do set changing numbers in tabular figures and keep 12px as the smallest size.
Do put a destructive choice in a dialog, in the destructive button style.
donts: Don't add a colour. No blue, no second accent, no status greens or ambers; state is ink, lime, or red for failure.
Don't set lime text on white or ground, or use lime for a button outside a solid ink surface.
Don't use shadows for lift, blur, glass, or gradients for tone. `box-shadow` is a zero-blur line or nothing.
Don't replace the handwriting with a spinner, skeleton, or stock progress illustration.
Don't imitate paper, notebooks or stationery, and don't drift toward a white-and-blue SaaS shell or a dark technical theme.
Don't introduce a third interface typeface, or use IBM Plex Sans KR below h1, or set interface text in the user's font.
Don't move the primary action out of the rail's bottom on a flow page.
Don't let an animation bounce, loop, or run longer than the thing it explains; the film's length is set by the steps, not by decoration.
